explanation: The capital of ancient Israel, destroyed by the Babylonians in Jeremiah 39.
An ancient city and empire in Mesopotamia, known for conquering Jerusalem and taking the Jews into exile.
King of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and took the Jews into exile.
A condition where a person or group is forced to leave their homeland and live in another country.
The last king of Judah, who was captured by Nebuchadnezzar and taken to Babylon.
A prophet in the Old Testament who delivered God's word and warned about Jerusalem's destruction.
The temple in Jerusalem, the center of Jewish faith and worship, destroyed by the Babylonians.
Destruction or collapse of something, as in this case referring to the fall of Jerusalem.
Fear and respect for God, often linked with obedience to God's will and commands.
